title: Sprint
description: A durable plan spanning sessions (D-0004). Epic-bounded, or a hotfix sprint promoted from a single issue. Not active until ratified by User. Source file: governance/sprints.json ({"entries": [Sprint]}).

epic.description: Null only when hotfix is true.

hotfix.description: Hotfix lane: single-task sprint promoted from an issue, no epic process.

source_issue.description: Required when hotfix is true — the issue that was promoted.

tasks.description: Every task added must carry a complete task_order (and a story, unless hotfix).

parallel.description: How many of this sprint's tasks may be in_progress at once (D-0084). Declared at planning because the sprint is the unit User ratifies, and changeable only while the sprint is `proposed` -- a change after ratification is a re-ratification. Absent means 1: every sprint written before D-0084 ran one task at a time, and a default is the honest reading of a field that did not exist. `--hotfix` is always 1.

authority.description: How the act was authorised. direct = a person said so in this session; app = taken through scrumux-app, which is the authority (User's ruling, 2026-08-28), where no dispatch session is involved -- a sprint ratification is opened at repo level and belongs to no session, and naming one would invent it; app:<session> = the same, for an act that DOES belong to a dispatched session; standing:D-XXXX = a ratified delegation, and the D- ref must resolve.

ratified.description: Present iff status has reached ratified. Names WHO ratified and on what authority. `by` used to default to a literal name in the CLI, which wrote it onto acts User did not take; it is now required. `authority` is required by the CLI for every NEW ratification but NOT by this schema: 27 ratifications here predate the field, and a schema that demanded it would force either a red repo for ever or a backfilled attestation nobody can stand behind. `records check` warns on the gap instead (2026-08-28).

descoped.description: Tasks removed from this sprint after ratification, each with the reason and date (T-0067). Removing UNWORKED work from a plan is a ruling; a task with log entries is refused, since removing it would rewrite the record. The reason names what changed and where the work went: "I-0112's read-side self-heal is a NEW capability and the freeze holds; the issue stays documented" rather than "out of scope", which only restates the act the plan already framed.

additions.description: Tasks added AFTER the sprint was ratified (D-S017). The addition is allowed and waits for its own ratification: `task brief` fails its sprint gate for the added task until `sprint ratify` ratifies the addition, and the tasks ratified with the sprint are unaffected. The sprint's own `ratified` block is never rewritten by an addition's ratification. Absent on every sprint written before the field, which therefore has no pending additions.

ratified.description: Null while the addition awaits ratification; then who ratified it, when, and on what authority (same vocabulary as the sprint's `ratified.authority`).
